sentences.en: The thing about Lindsey Graham is he's one of these figures in Washington that comes with kind of a nonverbal reaction at this point.
sentences.zh: 关于林赛·格雷厄姆，有一点是，他是华盛顿特区那种现在一提到名字就会让人产生某种非语言反应的人物。

sentences.en: Mark Leibovich wrote about Graham for The New York Times magazine.
sentences.zh: 马克·莱博维奇曾为《纽约时报》杂志撰写过关于格雷厄姆的文章。

sentences.en: You mention his name any time over the last six months to 12 months, and you get this combination grimace, shrug, follow-up question.
sentences.zh: 在过去六到十二个月里，你只要提到他的名字，人们就会做出一种结合了皱眉、耸肩和追问的反应。

sentences.en: Yeah, what's going on?
sentences.zh: 是啊，到底怎么回事？

sentences.en: And in all the sort of Trump-era Republican mysteries, when we ask ourselves, what happened to this person?
sentences.zh: 在特朗普时代的各种共和党谜团中，当我们问自己：这个人到底怎么了？

sentences.en: Why is this person changing his or her mind so much now about Donald Trump?
sentences.zh: 为什么这个人现在对唐纳德·特朗普的态度发生了如此大的转变？

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham kind of is the signature mystery of the Trump era as far as what these conversions look like.
sentences.zh: 就这种转变而言，林赛·格雷厄姆算是特朗普时代最具代表性的谜团。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham grew up in a very small town in South Carolina, the town of central South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆在南卡罗来纳州的一个非常小的城镇长大，那是南卡罗来纳州中部的一个小镇。

sentences.en: And his parents owned a bar there called the Sanitary Cafe.
sentences.zh: 他的父母在那里开了一家叫“卫生咖啡馆”的酒吧。

sentences.en: And not only did they own it, but they lived in an apartment right behind the bar.
sentences.zh: 他们不仅拥有这家店，还住在酒吧后面的一间公寓里。

sentences.en: They shared a restroom with the patrons of the bar.
sentences.zh: 他们和酒吧的顾客共用一个洗手间。

sentences.en: And he went from there.
sentences.zh: 他就是从那里走出来的。

sentences.en: He was the first member of his family to go to college.
sentences.zh: 他是家里第一个上大学的人。

sentences.en: His parents died when he was in his early 20s.
sentences.zh: 他20出头时父母就去世了。

sentences.en: He joined the military.
sentences.zh: 他加入了军队。

sentences.en: He eventually got into politics and then was elected to Congress and eventually was elected to the Senate.
sentences.zh: 后来他投身政界，当选为国会议员，最终当选为参议员。

sentences.en: Where over the years he's become known as kind of a reliable, conservative, pretty partisan Republican.
sentences.zh: 多年来，他一直被视为那种可靠、保守、党派色彩浓厚的共和党人。

sentences.en: I'm Lindsey Graham and I approve this message.
sentences.zh: 我是林赛·格雷厄姆，我支持这条信息。

sentences.en: Through the Bush years.
sentences.zh: 在布什执政期间。

sentences.en: He closed Obamacare from day one.
sentences.zh: 他从第一天起就反对奥巴马医改。

sentences.en: Voting against it.
sentences.zh: 投票反对它。

sentences.en: Through the Obama years.
sentences.zh: 在奥巴马执政期间。

sentences.en: He led the fight on Benghazi.
sentences.zh: 他领导了针对班加西事件的斗争。

sentences.en: Demanding answers.
sentences.zh: 要求给出答案。

sentences.en: He was known as someone who was a truth teller within his caucus.
sentences.zh: 他曾被认为是党团内部敢说真话的人。

sentences.en: He's been a champion for our military, our veterans, and a fighter for South Carolina jobs.
sentences.zh: 他一直是我们的军队、退伍军人的捍卫者，也是南卡罗来纳州就业机会的争取者。

sentences.en: He was seen, much like McCain was, as someone who you could have a conversation with, who you could deal with.
sentences.zh: 就像麦凯恩一样，他被视为一个可以与之交谈、可以与之共事的人。

sentences.en: All eyes on Lindsey Graham and another Democratic member trying to come up with some sort of bipartisan compromise.
sentences.zh: 所有人的目光都集中在林赛·格雷厄姆和另一位试图达成某种两党妥协的民主党议员身上。

sentences.en: And really won a lot of bipartisan respect, a lot of respect across the aisles.
sentences.zh: 他确实赢得了许多两党尊重，赢得了跨党派的尊重。

sentences.en: Took on some pretty unpopular issues within his caucus.
sentences.zh: 他承担了一些在党团内部非常不受欢迎的议题。

sentences.en: Like what?

sentences.zh: 80%的人希望开始修复破碎的移民系统。

sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他曾是个了不起的交易撮合者。

sentences.en: He, to this day, is remembered, and remembered is sort of a key word because it's very past tense,
sentences.zh: 直到今天，人们还记得他——“记得”这个词很关键，因为这已经是过去式了——

sentences.en: as someone who could speak some truth to power and someone who was seen as a reasonable, independent conservative.
sentences.zh: 他曾被视为一个敢于对权势说真话的人，一个理性的、独立的保守派。

sentences.en: Let me tell you about Senator McCain.
sentences.zh: 让我来告诉你关于麦凯恩参议员的事。

sentences.en: And he also was like a sidekick, kind of the Gilligan to John McCain's skipper.
sentences.zh: 他当时就像个跟班，有点像约翰·麦凯恩船长身边的吉利根。

sentences.en: He would die for this country.
sentences.zh: 他会为这个国家牺牲。

sentences.en: I love him to death.
sentences.zh: 我爱死他了。

sentences.en: He was always his side.
sentences.zh: 他总是站在他那边。

sentences.en: The two of them had sort of similar senses of humor.
sentences.zh: 他们俩有种相似的幽默感。

sentences.en: The reason why Lindsey is not married is because he can't find anyone that loves him as much as he does.
sentences.zh: 林赛之所以没结婚，是因为他找不到像他爱自己那样爱他的人。

sentences.en: And was always, again, very derivative of the energy that John McCain brought to everything that John McCain did.

sentences.zh: 有人问他，你知道，约翰·麦凯恩是英雄吗？

sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普说，不，他不是。

sentences.en: I like people who weren't captured.

sentences.zh: 我不需要民调来告诉唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.zh: 说约翰·麦凯恩是个失败者是不对的，因为他在战争期间被俘了。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham, as John McCain's best friend, was extremely, you know, took great umbrage at this.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆作为约翰·麦凯恩最好的朋友，对此感到非常愤怒。

sentences.en: Predictably, the crank calls, the threats commenced immediately on Lindsey Graham's cell phone.
sentences.zh: 不出所料，骚扰电话和威胁立即涌向了林赛·格雷厄姆的手机。

sentences.en: I think he's a kook.
sentences.zh: 我觉得他是个怪人。

sentences.zh: 我觉得他疯了。

sentences.zh: 我觉得他不适合担任公职。

sentences.en: So the phone thing happens.

sentences.en: The relationship did not improve over the course of the campaign.
sentences.zh: 在竞选过程中，他们的关系并没有改善。

sentences.en: He's a race-baiting, xenophobic, religious bigot.
sentences.zh: 他是个煽动种族主义、仇外、宗教偏执的人。

sentences.en: To say the leaSt.

sentences.en: And then even when Donald Trump was elected, even when he became president, Lindsey Graham and John McCain were still none too happy with the fact that Donald Trump was president.
sentences.zh: 即使在唐纳德·特朗普当选，甚至成为总统后，林赛·格雷厄姆和约翰·麦凯恩对唐纳德·特朗普担任总统的事实仍然很不高兴。

sentences.en: They kind of held their powder for a while.

sentences.en: But there were certain occasions where Lindsey Graham was actually quite vocal and really wasn't trying to hide his feelings at all.
sentences.zh: 但在某些场合，林赛·格雷厄姆确实非常直言不讳，根本没有试图掩饰自己的感受。

sentences.zh: 在夏洛茨维尔示威游行并最终发生谋杀案之后。

sentences.zh: 如果我是美国总统，而这些人对我及我的议程表示同情，我会感到困扰。

sentences.en: And I would urge the president to dissuade them of the fact that he's sympathetic to their cause.
sentences.zh: 我会敦促总统打消他们认为他同情其事业的想法。

sentences.en: Because their cause is hate.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的事业是仇恨。

sentences.en: It is un-American.
sentences.zh: 这是反美国的。

sentences.zh: 他们是国内恐怖分子。

sentences.zh: 在这个问题上，我们需要总统做更多的事情。

sentences.en: And the president seemed to side with President Putin over the conclusion of his own intelligence that Russia meddled with the election of 2016.

sentences.en: He's misjudging Putin.

sentences.en: I don't think he was prepared as well as he should have been.

sentences.zh: 我自己也曾这样问过。

sentences.zh: 很高兴见到你。

sentences.en: Pull up the chair.
sentences.zh: 拉把椅子过来。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: So, Mark, where did you start your conversation with Graham?
sentences.zh: 那么，马克，你是从哪里开始和格雷厄姆对话的？

sentences.en: So this is just, I figure I'd start with this.
sentences.zh: 我想，我就从这里开始吧。

sentences.en: I mean, since...
sentences.zh: 我是说，自从……

sentences.en: I asked Lindsey Graham how he was getting along without John McCain.
sentences.zh: 我问林赛·格雷厄姆，没有了约翰·麦凯恩，他过得怎么样。

sentences.en: I miss John.
sentences.zh: 我想念约翰。

sentences.en: I miss him a lot.
sentences.zh: 我非常想念他。

sentences.en: I mean, I hadn't seen him since John McCain had passed away, which would have been in AuguSt.
sentences.zh: 我是说，自从约翰·麦凯恩八月份去世后，我就没再见过他。

sentences.en: I still, on occasion, want to pick up the phone and call.
sentences.zh: 我有时还是想拿起电话打给他。

sentences.en: So it was a relationship that was like a political marriage.
sentences.zh: 所以，那是一种类似于政治婚姻的关系。

sentences.en: And he said he was doing okay.
sentences.zh: 他说他过得还行。

sentences.en: He misses him.
sentences.zh: 他很想念他。

sentences.en: He thinks about him all the time.
sentences.zh: 他无时无刻不在想他。

sentences.en: You know, he loved the conteSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他热爱竞争。

sentences.en: He loved being relevant.
sentences.zh: 他热爱那种身处核心的感觉。

sentences.en: He kept himself relevant.
sentences.zh: 他让自己始终保持在核心位置。

sentences.en: But from there, he jumped immediately to how John McCain made him feel, which was relevant.
sentences.zh: 但从那之后，他立刻跳到了约翰·麦凯恩带给他的感觉，那就是——身处核心。

sentences.en: Yeah, and I like being relevant.
sentences.zh: 是的，我喜欢身处核心。

sentences.en: And the way you stay relevant is you stay engaged.
sentences.zh: 而保持核心地位的方法就是保持参与。

sentences.en: There's a lot of space here to take on tough issues because most people shy away from them.
sentences.zh: 这里有很大的空间去处理棘手的问题，因为大多数人都会避开它们。

sentences.en: So Lindsey Graham said, like, John and I were relevant together.
sentences.zh: 所以林赛·格雷厄姆说，约翰和我在一起时，我们都是核心人物。

sentences.en: I mean, it was like we're sharing a meal together.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，就像我们在一起吃饭一样。

sentences.en: We're sharing a value system together.
sentences.zh: 我们共享着一套价值观。

sentences.en: And that value system was relevance.
sentences.zh: 而那套价值观就是“核心地位”。

sentences.en: And I was confused by the word.
sentences.zh: 我被这个词搞糊涂了。

sentences.en: I said, what do you mean by that?
sentences.zh: 我说，你这话是什么意思？

sentences.en: And he said relevant is like in the middle of everything.
sentences.zh: 他说，核心就是处于一切事物的中心。

sentences.en: Relevant is you're making a difference.
sentences.zh: 核心就是你在发挥作用。

sentences.en: It means that during the time in which you possess political influence and power, use it.
sentences.zh: 这意味着在你拥有政治影响力和权力的这段时间里，要好好利用它。

sentences.en: John McCain was always surrounded by an entourage.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦凯恩总是被随从簇拥着。

sentences.en: He was always surrounded by cameras.
sentences.zh: 他总是被摄像机包围着。

sentences.en: He was always surrounded by a sense that because John McCain was there, something momentous was happening.
sentences.zh: 他总是被一种感觉所包围，那就是因为约翰·麦凯恩在场，重大的事情正在发生。

sentences.en: And Lindsey Graham, by virtue of residency in that orbit, was able to reap that also.
sentences.zh: 而林赛·格雷厄姆凭借身处那个轨道，也能够从中获益。

sentences.en: And so how does Graham explain to you how his relationship with Trump develops and how this evolution kind of lands with him having a relationship with Trump?
sentences.zh: 那么，格雷厄姆是如何向你解释他与特朗普的关系是如何发展的，以及这种演变是如何让他与特朗普建立起关系的？

sentences.en: I was calling Trump a race-betting, religious, xenophobic.
sentences.zh: 我曾称特朗普为种族歧视、宗教偏执、排外的人。

sentences.en: Did you mean that when you said that stuff about Trump?
sentences.zh: 你说那些关于特朗普的话时，是认真的吗？

sentences.en: Oh, I thought – yeah, I didn't vote for him.
sentences.zh: 哦，我想——是的，我没投他的票。

sentences.en: I thought his campaign was – You didn't vote for him in general?
sentences.zh: 我觉得他的竞选活动是——你大选时没投他？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Who did you vote for?
sentences.zh: 你投给了谁？

sentences.en: I vote for Evan – whatever the guy's name is.
sentences.zh: 我投给了埃文——不管那家伙叫什么名字。

sentences.en: What knows who walked in the door?
sentences.zh: 谁知道走进门的是谁？

sentences.en: That dude.
sentences.zh: 那家伙。

sentences.en: So – but I loSt.
sentences.zh: 所以——但我输了。

sentences.en: I mean, the people have spoken.
sentences.zh: 我是说，人民已经发声了。

sentences.en: So, okay, let's see how we can help this guy be a good president.
sentences.zh: 所以，好吧，让我们看看如何能帮这家伙成为一名好总统。

sentences.en: I think he knew intuitively that he needed to build a relationship fairly quickly, you know,
sentences.zh: 我想他凭直觉知道他需要相当快地建立起一种关系，你知道，

sentences.en: in part because of political realities in South Carolina and the fact of his re-election coming up in 2020.
sentences.zh: 部分原因是南卡罗来纳州的政治现实，以及他即将在2020年面临连任的事实。

sentences.en: But – I didn't call him.
sentences.zh: 但是——我没给他打电话。

sentences.en: So he called me about six weeks after.
sentences.zh: 所以他在六周后给我打了电话。

sentences.en: And he said, let's talk.
sentences.zh: 他说，我们谈谈吧。

sentences.en: Donald Trump sort of short-circuited the process by calling him firSt.
sentences.zh: 唐纳德·特朗普通过先给他打电话，某种程度上绕过了那个过程。

sentences.en: He says, I don't have your phone number.
sentences.zh: 他说，我没有你的电话号码。

sentences.en: And I said, there's a reason for that.
sentences.zh: 我说，那是有原因的。

sentences.en: And I didn't lie.
sentences.zh: 我没撒谎。

sentences.en: Because I had to throw it out because you ruined it.
sentences.zh: 因为我不得不把它删了，因为你把它毁了。

sentences.en: And yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And then – Then he took me to the place right off – the Oval Office and we had lunch.
sentences.zh: 然后——然后他带我去了椭圆形办公室旁边的地方，我们吃了午饭。

sentences.en: And we talked for an hour.
sentences.zh: 我们谈了一个小时。

sentences.en: He really seemed to care what I think.
sentences.zh: 他似乎真的很在意我的想法。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: What I thought.
sentences.zh: 我的想法。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he said, you know, I know we've had our differences, but I'd like you to help me.
sentences.zh: 他说，你知道，我知道我们之间有分歧，但我希望你能帮我。

sentences.en: I said, I'll be glad to help you.
sentences.zh: 我说，我很乐意帮你。

sentences.en: I want you to be successful.
sentences.zh: 我希望你成功。

sentences.en: Do you like him on a superficial, like we golf together, we have a little rapport level?
sentences.zh: 你喜欢他吗？是在那种肤浅的，比如我们一起打高尔夫，有点交情的层面上？

sentences.en: Let me tell you this.
sentences.zh: 让我告诉你这个。

sentences.en: That's what's changed.
sentences.zh: 这就是改变的地方。

sentences.en: So you feel like genuine –
sentences.zh: 所以你觉得是真诚的——

sentences.en: Well, so, and I don't want to be Sigmund Freud, he's got a tough job.
sentences.zh: 嗯，而且我不想当西格蒙德·弗洛伊德，他的工作很艰巨。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: I mean, he doesn't have a whole group of old friends.
sentences.zh: 我是说，他身边没有一群老朋友。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: The guy who's president of the United States.
sentences.zh: 那个担任美国总统的人。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: This stuff is coming at him at Mach 2 and 3.
sentences.zh: 这些事情正以两三倍音速向他袭来。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: He feels completely under siege, you know, from the Mueller stuff.
sentences.zh: 他感觉自己完全被围困了，你知道，因为穆勒调查的事。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And he is trying to navigate all the things that come with being Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 他正在努力应对作为唐纳德·特朗普所带来的一切。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: But there's a side to him that I'm pulling for him now.
sentences.zh: 但他有让我现在支持他的一面。

sentences.en: Mm-hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯哼。

sentences.en: Does that make sense?
sentences.zh: 这说得通吗？

sentences.en: Were you before?
sentences.zh: 你以前支持吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Like, meaning – but give me a time frame.
sentences.zh: 比如，意思是——但给我一个时间范围。

sentences.en: A couple weeks ago?
sentences.zh: 几周前？

sentences.en: I think it's been the last year.
sentences.zh: 我想是过去这一年。

sentences.en: Really?
sentences.zh: 真的吗？

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Well, so what actually happens in the past year between Lindsey Graham and President Trump that explains this?
sentences.zh: 那么，过去一年里林赛·格雷厄姆和特朗普总统之间到底发生了什么，能解释这一切？

sentences.en: They're spending a lot of time together.
sentences.zh: 他们花了很多时间在一起。

sentences.en: I've never been called this much by a president in my life.
sentences.zh: 我这辈子从来没被总统打过这么多电话。

sentences.en: Is that – what's that like?
sentences.zh: 那是——那是什么感觉？

sentences.en: It's weird and it's flattering.
sentences.zh: 很奇怪，但也受宠若惊。

sentences.en: And the time they're spending together, the votes Lindsey Graham is casting for the Trump agenda.
sentences.zh: 他们在一起花时间，林赛·格雷厄姆为特朗普的议程投票。

sentences.en: The judges have been good.
sentences.zh: 法官们选得不错。

sentences.en: The tax cuts, deregulation, all this work.
sentences.zh: 减税、放松管制，所有这些工作。

sentences.en: He's rebuilt the military.
sentences.zh: 他重建了军队。

sentences.en: Whether on tax reform, whether on repealing the Affordable Care Act, that was both in 2017, but into 2018 on foreign policy.
sentences.zh: 无论是在税改，还是在废除《平价医疗法案》上，那都是2017年的事，但到了2018年，在外交政策上也是如此。

sentences.en: I'm hoping through him that we can do some things in North Korea that maybe we couldn't have done otherwise.
sentences.zh: 我希望通过他，我们能在朝鲜做一些以前可能做不到的事情。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham has certainly ascended to the role of, you know, one of Donald Trump's two or three closest advisors on the Hill.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆无疑已经晋升为唐纳德·特朗普在国会山最亲密的二三位顾问之一。

sentences.en: The backdrop to this, though, is that Lindsey Graham's best friend, John McCain, is going through a very, very public, difficult illness.
sentences.zh: 然而，这一切的背景是，林赛·格雷厄姆最好的朋友约翰·麦凯恩正在经历一场非常、非常公开且艰难的疾病。

sentences.en: And Donald Trump basically didn't let up at all.
sentences.zh: 而唐纳德·特朗普基本上一点也没有收手。

sentences.en: He was still criticizing John McCain for his vote against the Affordable Care Act repeal of 2017.
sentences.zh: 他仍然因为约翰·麦凯恩在2017年投票反对废除《平价医疗法案》而批评他。

sentences.en: But also, John McCain, through his office, even through his illness, was not shy about criticizing Donald Trump for things like Helsinki, Charlottesville.
sentences.zh: 但同时，约翰·麦凯恩通过他的办公室，甚至在患病期间，也毫不避讳地批评唐纳德·特朗普在赫尔辛基、夏洛茨维尔等事件上的表现。

sentences.en: And Donald Trump was not one to let this lie and was going to bash John McCain right back.
sentences.zh: 而唐纳德·特朗普也不是那种会善罢甘休的人，他会反过来抨击约翰·麦凯恩。

sentences.en: So you had this situation where Lindsey Graham and the president were becoming very close and public friends, whereas John McCain was dying a very,
sentences.zh: 所以你面临这样一种情况：林赛·格雷厄姆和总统成了非常亲密的公开朋友，而约翰·麦凯恩却正在经历一场非常、

sentences.en: very slow and tragic and public death.
sentences.zh: 非常缓慢、悲惨且公开的死亡。

sentences.en: So I think people began to ask this question, what was going on with Lindsey Graham, in maybe a more personal framework, because John McCain and he were known to be so close.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为人们开始问这个问题，林赛·格雷厄姆到底怎么了，也许是在一个更个人的框架下，因为约翰·麦凯恩和他众所周知非常亲密。

sentences.en: And John McCain obviously was very sick.
sentences.zh: 而且约翰·麦凯恩显然病得很重。

sentences.en: And I wonder, did you ask Graham about how McCain felt about this developing relationship between Graham and Trump, considering their past and McCain's place in it?
sentences.zh: 我想知道，你有没有问过格雷厄姆，麦凯恩对格雷厄姆和特朗普之间这种发展的关系有何感想，考虑到他们的过去以及麦凯恩在其中的地位？

sentences.en: Yeah, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我问了。

sentences.en: Here's what I told John.
sentences.zh: 我是这样告诉约翰的。

sentences.en: He's president.
sentences.zh: 他是总统。

sentences.en: And I've seen you, once the election was over, embrace people.
sentences.zh: 我见过你，一旦选举结束，你就会拥抱人们。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: And that's what I admired the most about you.
sentences.zh: 那是我最钦佩你的地方。

sentences.en: And, you know, if you could go to Vietnam and forgive him, anybody could.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，如果你能去越南并原谅他们，任何人都可以。

sentences.en: Sure.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: If you could work with Obama, anybody could.
sentences.zh: 如果你能和奥巴马合作，任何人都可以。

sentences.en: And I want to stay in this guy's orbit.
sentences.zh: 我想留在这个人的轨道里。

sentences.en: So, in a way, you're reminding John McCain of his own example, but also appealing to the ego that John McCain obviously had in very, very high measure.
sentences.zh: 所以，在某种程度上，你是在提醒约翰·麦凯恩他自己的榜样，同时也诉诸于约翰·麦凯恩显然拥有极高程度的自尊心。

sentences.en: And do you know if McCain essentially blessed this or said, I understand, Lindsey?
sentences.zh: 你知道麦凯恩是否基本上认可了这一点，或者说，我理解，林赛？

sentences.en: I don't think he blessed it.
sentences.zh: 我不认为他认可了。

sentences.en: I think that's probably too strong, but I think John McCain, as well as anyone, understands politics.
sentences.zh: 我觉得这个词可能太重了，但我认为约翰·麦凯恩比任何人都更懂政治。

sentences.en: Also, look, he had other things to worry about.
sentences.zh: 再说，看，他还有别的事情要担心。

sentences.en: He was dying.
sentences.zh: 他快要去世了。

sentences.en: He was sort of getting his legacy and his affairs in order.
sentences.zh: 他当时正在整理他的遗产和事务。

sentences.en: He was not at his best in the last year of his life when he was battling brain cancer and so forth.
sentences.zh: 在他生命的最后一年，当他与脑癌等疾病作斗争时，他的状态并不好。

sentences.en: So, what I've done for Trump is, I don't think, inconsistent with what I've done with others.
sentences.zh: 所以，我为特朗普所做的事情，我不认为与我为其他人所做的事情不一致。

sentences.en: But here's the difference.
sentences.zh: 但区别在于这里。

sentences.en: The difference is more important and he's receptive.
sentences.zh: 区别在于这更重要，而且他很乐于接受。

sentences.en: So, John McCain passes away in August and then just a few weeks later, you had the crescendo of the Brett Kavanaugh hearings.
sentences.zh: 所以，约翰·麦凯恩在八月去世了，几周后，布雷特·卡瓦诺的听证会达到了高潮。

sentences.en: I mean, we all remember, you know, a very, very powerful day where there was a sense for about, you know, maybe two-thirds of the day that Justice Kavanaugh was in real trouble,
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我们都记得，你知道，那是非常、非常震撼的一天，大约有三分之二的时间，人们觉得卡瓦诺大法官真的有大麻烦了，

sentences.en: that Dr. Ford's story was extremely compelling.
sentences.zh: 福特博士的故事非常有说服力。

sentences.en: Then, all of a sudden, Republicans on the committee were speaking and Lindsey Graham gave this real show-stopping speech.
sentences.zh: 然后，突然之间，委员会的共和党人开始发言，林赛·格雷厄姆发表了那场真正令人叹为观止的演讲。

sentences.en: This is the most unethical sham since I've been in politics.
sentences.zh: 这是我从政以来见过的最不道德的骗局。

sentences.en: And if you really wanted to know the truth, you sure as hell wouldn't have done what you've done to this guy.
sentences.zh: 如果你真的想知道真相，你绝不可能对这家伙做出这种事。

sentences.en: That, at the moment, you know, people thought, you know, might have really changed the momentum of this thing.
sentences.zh: 当时，你知道，人们以为，你知道，这可能会真正改变这件事的势头。

sentences.en: Boy, y'all want power.
sentences.zh: 天哪，你们这些人真是渴望权力。

sentences.en: God, I hope you never get it.
sentences.zh: 上帝啊，我希望你们永远得不到它。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: In which he essentially assails the Democratic members of the committee for basically being power-hungry and soulless.
sentences.zh: 他在文中主要抨击了委员会的民主党成员，认为他们本质上是贪权且没有灵魂的。

sentences.en: Power-hungry and smearing and ruining Brett Kavanaugh's life.
sentences.zh: 贪权，还抹黑并毁掉了布雷特·卡瓦诺的生活。

sentences.en: Did you feel like in any way you had an audience in the White House?
sentences.zh: 你是否觉得自己在某种程度上在白宫有听众？

sentences.en: I mean, were you thinking there was not an audience?
sentences.zh: 我是说，你当时在想没有听众吗？

sentences.en: I was pissed at everybody on the other side.
sentences.zh: 我对另一边的每个人都感到愤怒。

sentences.en: Genuinely.
sentences.zh: 真心话。

sentences.en: It was just like, okay, I voted for your guys.
sentences.zh: 当时的感觉就是，好吧，我投了你们的人。

sentences.en: What's going on here?
sentences.zh: 这到底是怎么回事？

sentences.en: I was furious for the way the guy was treated.
sentences.zh: 我对这家伙受到的对待感到愤怒。

sentences.en: And I've had a very fixed view about the law.
sentences.zh: 而且我对法律一直有着非常固定的看法。

sentences.en: I mean, that's been my life.
sentences.zh: 我是说，那一直是我的人生。

sentences.en: And I just think, you know, I don't want to ruin the judiciary because we can't get along up here.
sentences.zh: 我只是觉得，你知道，我不想毁掉司法机构，因为我们在这里无法和睦相处。

sentences.en: It was a very pitched and partisan setting, obviously.
sentences.zh: 显然，那是一个非常激烈且党派色彩浓厚的环境。

sentences.en: I think the collateral damage there is what it did to his reputation across the aisle, which has not been repaired yet.
sentences.zh: 我认为那里的附带损害是他对两党声誉的影响，至今尚未修复。

sentences.en: But in a sense, that sort of played to some very, very strong suits that Lindsey Graham had,
sentences.zh: 但从某种意义上说，这在某种程度上迎合了林赛·格雷厄姆非常、非常强项的地方，

sentences.en: beginning with being something that was delightful to the president of the United States and his base.
sentences.zh: 首先就是做一些让美国总统及其基本盘感到高兴的事情。

sentences.en: The thing I like about the president is that he has allowed me in that space.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢总统的一点是，他允许我进入那个空间。

sentences.en: And after Kavanaugh, it's even been more.
sentences.zh: 而在卡瓦诺事件之后，这种空间甚至更大了。

sentences.en: I can imagine.
sentences.zh: 我可以想象。

sentences.en: He likes a fighter.
sentences.zh: 他喜欢斗士。

sentences.en: After the Kavanaugh hearings, I think the question that everybody has on some low level about what happened to Graham is now the question we're all openly asking.
sentences.zh: 在卡瓦诺听证会之后，我认为每个人在某种程度上对格雷厄姆身上发生的事情所持有的疑问，现在是我们所有人都在公开提出的问题。

sentences.en: What happened to Lindsey Graham?
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆到底怎么了？

sentences.en: So did you actually pose that question?
sentences.zh: 那么你真的提出了这个问题吗？

sentences.en: Yes, I did.
sentences.zh: 是的，我提了。

sentences.en: You seem a little sick and tired of the what's happening to Lindsey Graham question.
sentences.zh: 你似乎对“林赛·格雷厄姆怎么了”这个问题感到有点厌烦了。

sentences.en: Yeah, well, it's just like, yeah, like, OK, nothing from my point of view.
sentences.zh: 是啊，嗯，就像是，是的，好吧，从我的角度来看，什么都没发生。

sentences.en: If you know anything about me, it'd be odd for me not to do this.
sentences.zh: 如果你了解我，我如果不这样做才奇怪呢。

sentences.en: Now, what is this?
sentences.zh: 那么，这是什么？

sentences.en: This is to try to be relevant.
sentences.zh: 这是为了努力保持相关性。

sentences.en: Try to be relevant.
sentences.zh: 努力保持相关性。

sentences.en: In a sense, he uses the notion of relevance as a catch-all.
sentences.zh: 从某种意义上说，他把相关性的概念当作了一个万能借口。

sentences.en: But to what end?
sentences.zh: 但目的是什么呢？

sentences.en: I mean, because you're on.
sentences.zh: 我是说，因为你在台上。

sentences.en: To the end, to the end, to the objectives that I want.
sentences.zh: 为了目的，为了目的，为了我想要实现的目标。

sentences.en: Look, the uncharitable way of describing this would be opportunism.
sentences.zh: 听着，用不厚道的说法来描述，这叫机会主义。

sentences.en: The charitable way of saying this would be influence.
sentences.zh: 用厚道的说法来描述，这叫影响力。

sentences.en: And the fact is, one of the central dynamics of Washington circa 2019, circa the Trump administration,
sentences.zh: 事实是，2019年左右、特朗普政府时期华盛顿的核心动态之一，

sentences.en: is that never has the decision point been so wrapped up in the mercurialness of one single person as it is right now in Donald Trump's orbit.
sentences.zh: 就是决策点从未像现在在唐纳德·特朗普的轨道中这样，如此紧密地与一个人的反复无常联系在一起。

sentences.en: And Lindsey Graham has made himself a part of that orbit.
sentences.zh: 而林赛·格雷厄姆已经让自己成为了那个轨道的一部分。

sentences.en: Now, it might not last beyond next week.
sentences.zh: 现在，这可能持续不到下周。

sentences.en: It might not last beyond his reelection.
sentences.zh: 这可能持续不到他连任之后。

sentences.en: Who knows where this is going to end?
sentences.zh: 谁知道这会以什么告终呢？

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham posed that question himself to me.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆本人就向我提出了这个问题。

sentences.en: But for now, he seems to think it's very, very advantageous for him politically.
sentences.zh: 但目前，他似乎认为这对他在政治上非常、非常有优势。

sentences.en: But I want to linger on that word opportunism.
sentences.zh: 但我还是想在“机会主义”这个词上多停留一会儿。

sentences.en: Because if you look at the chronology, one view, and perhaps it's the most cynical view, is that Lindsey Graham, in the name of relevance,
sentences.zh: 因为如果你看看时间线，一种观点，也许是最愤世嫉俗的观点，是林赛·格雷厄姆以保持相关性为名，

sentences.en: attached himself to the biggest star in Republican politics for a very long time, and that was Senator John McCain.
sentences.zh: 长期依附于共和党政治中最大的明星，那就是约翰·麦凯恩参议员。

sentences.en: And then when Senator John McCain declines and ultimately dies, Lindsey Graham looks for the next biggest star to attach himself to, and that happens to be Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 然后当约翰·麦凯恩参议员衰落并最终去世时，林赛·格雷厄姆寻找下一个最大的明星来依附，而那个人恰好是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: And so despite the fact that these two men disdain each other and represent very different sides of the Republican Party, the constant is Lindsey Graham seeking out the star.
sentences.zh: 所以尽管这两个人互相鄙视，并且代表了共和党非常不同的派别，但不变的是林赛·格雷厄姆一直在寻找明星。

sentences.en: It is.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And at one point, I just sort of, like, blurted out, do you trust him?
sentences.zh: 有一次，我只是脱口而出，你信任他吗？

sentences.en: Meaning the president.
sentences.zh: 指的是总统。

sentences.en: And it took him a while to answer.
sentences.zh: 他花了一会儿才回答。

sentences.en: He seemed taken aback by that.
sentences.zh: 他似乎对这个问题感到吃惊。

sentences.en: And what he said was, I trust him to want to be successful, which, you know, is kind of a non-answer.
sentences.zh: 他说的是，我信任他想要获得成功，你知道，这算是一种非回答。

sentences.en: I mean, what president doesn't want to be successful, right?
sentences.zh: 我是说，哪个总统不想成功呢，对吧？

sentences.en: I mean, I think if I were to ask him, do you trust John McCain, he would say,
sentences.zh: 我是说，我想如果我问他，你信任约翰·麦凯恩吗，他会说，

sentences.en: I trust John McCain to love America and to always do what is right for America and to always work for a cause greater than himself.
sentences.zh: 我信任约翰·麦凯恩热爱美国，总是为美国做正确的事，总是为比他自身更伟大的事业而奋斗。

sentences.en: I remember asking him at one point, do you think Donald Trump believes in a cause greater than himself?
sentences.zh: 我记得有一次问他，你认为唐纳德·特朗普相信比他自身更伟大的事业吗？

sentences.en: And he said something to the effect that, well, Donald Trump's a showman.
sentences.zh: 他说了一些大意是，嗯，唐纳德·特朗普是个表演家。

sentences.en: He's a larger-than-life figure.
sentences.zh: 他是一个超越常人的人物。

sentences.en: He wants to be successful.
sentences.zh: 他想要成功。

sentences.en: Look, there are a lot of people who say, you know, Lindsey, you know better.
sentences.zh: 听着，有很多人说，你知道，林赛，你明明知道真相。

sentences.en: How can you live with yourself?
sentences.zh: 你怎么能心安理得地生活？

sentences.en: What are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你在做什么？

sentences.en: And he couches it in the virtue of, look, I believe very strongly in certain things around Syria, around Afghanistan, around judges.
sentences.zh: 他用一种美德来掩饰，看，我非常坚定地相信关于叙利亚、阿富汗、法官的某些事情。

sentences.en: That it is about outcomes.
sentences.zh: 这是关于结果的。

sentences.en: That I've got an opportunity up here working with the president to get some outcomes that could be really good for the country.
sentences.zh: 我在这里有机会与总统合作，取得一些对国家真正有好处的结果。

sentences.en: And I think, from my point of view, good for the world.
sentences.zh: 而且我认为，从我的角度来看，对世界也有好处。

sentences.en: Being relevant to Donald Trump, being in his orbit, helps me influence the things that I think are good for our country.
sentences.zh: 与唐纳德·特朗普保持相关性，进入他的轨道，有助于我影响那些我认为对我们国家有益的事情。

sentences.en: And good for your re-election.
sentences.zh: 还有对你的连任有益。

sentences.en: I cynically said, and also good for Lindsey Graham's re-election.
sentences.zh: 我愤世嫉俗地说，也对林赛·格雷厄姆的连任有益。

sentences.en: Yeah, I mean, if you don't want to get re-elected, you're in the wrong business.
sentences.zh: 是啊，我是说，如果你不想连任，那你入错行了。

sentences.en: He sort of glibly said, well, if you don't want to be re-elected, you're in the wrong business.
sentences.zh: 他轻率地说，嗯，如果你不想连任，那你入错行了。

sentences.en: I mean, this question of what is going on with Lindsey Graham is so present around him.
sentences.zh: 我是说，关于林赛·格雷厄姆到底怎么了的问题，在他周围如此普遍。

sentences.en: It's come to define him so much that he felt completely at home, even raising the question rhetorically on the stump in South Carolina.
sentences.zh: 它已经定义了他，以至于他在南卡罗来纳州的竞选集会上，甚至觉得可以完全自然地提出这个问题。

sentences.en: There was a Republican lunch we went to in Greenville, where he was saying, what happened to me?
sentences.zh: 我们在格林维尔参加过一次共和党午餐会，他在会上说，我怎么了？

sentences.en: And he said it twice.
sentences.zh: 他说了两次。

sentences.en: And he said, what's happened to Lindsey Graham?
sentences.zh: 他说，林赛·格雷厄姆怎么了？

sentences.en: Not a damn thing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没发生。

sentences.en: Not a damn thing.
sentences.zh: 什么都没发生。

sentences.en: And people kind of, like, nodded knowingly.
sentences.zh: 人们有点心照不宣地点了点头。

sentences.en: And what he was doing was sort of owning the question.
sentences.zh: 他所做的是在某种程度上承认这个问题。

sentences.en: He was sort of taking it as a part of his political identity.
sentences.zh: 他把它当作自己政治身份的一部分。

sentences.en: But at the same time, he was being defiant about it, too.
sentences.zh: 但与此同时，他也对此表现得非常挑衅。

sentences.en: And he kept talking about how, like, look, all the smart people in Washington, they hate us.
sentences.zh: 他不停地说，看，华盛顿所有那些聪明人，他们讨厌我们。

sentences.en: The people in the media, they hate us.
sentences.zh: 媒体里的人，他们讨厌我们。

sentences.en: You know, they hate him, him being Donald Trump.
sentences.zh: 你知道，他们讨厌他，他就是唐纳德·特朗普。

sentences.en: You know, essentially, it's sort of an old populist refrain, which is they don't—they look down on our way in life.
sentences.zh: 你知道，本质上，这是一种旧的民粹主义副歌，就是他们不——他们看不起我们的生活方式。

sentences.en: Literally the next day in his office in Washington, he was talking about how you showcase your issues.
sentences.zh: 就在第二天，他在华盛顿的办公室里，谈论如何展示你的议题。

sentences.en: This is what you do when you're running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 这就是你竞选连任时所做的事情。

sentences.en: He was becoming one of the smart people.
sentences.zh: 他正在成为那些聪明人之一。

sentences.en: He was talking to me, wise guy to wise guy.
sentences.zh: 他是在跟我说话，聪明人对聪明人。

sentences.en: And he was essentially giving away the game as if, you know, his Senate office in Washington and a luncheon hall in Greenville, South Carolina,
sentences.zh: 他本质上是在泄露游戏的秘密，就好像，你知道，他在华盛顿的参议院办公室和南卡罗来纳州格林维尔的午餐大厅，

sentences.en: were completely different worlds that have nothing to do with each other.
sentences.zh: 是完全不同的世界，彼此毫无关系。

sentences.en: And it sounds like at the end of the day, he is being honest in the sense that nothing did happen to him.
sentences.zh: 听起来归根结底，他是诚实的，因为确实什么都没发生在他身上。

sentences.en: He is the same guy.
sentences.zh: 他还是同一个人。

sentences.en: Yeah, here's the thing.
sentences.zh: 是啊，事情是这样的。

sentences.en: I was pretty struck by how honest, how candid he was in talking about what his game was, what he was doing.
sentences.zh: 他谈论他的游戏是什么，他在做什么时表现出的诚实和坦率，让我印象深刻。

sentences.en: Him explicitly saying, you showcase your issues, meaning you say certain things when you're running for re-election, essentially.
sentences.zh: 他明确说，你展示你的议题，意思是你在竞选连任时会说某些话，本质上是这样。

sentences.en: To certain audiences.
sentences.zh: 对特定的受众。

sentences.en: To certain audiences.
sentences.zh: 对特定的受众。

sentences.en: He said facetiously, but not really facetiously, you know, you recall that in 2010,
sentences.zh: 他半开玩笑地说，但也不完全是开玩笑，你知道，你记得在2010年，

sentences.en: John McCain turned himself into the most conservative senator in the Senate when he was running for re-election in 2010.
sentences.zh: 约翰·麦凯恩在2010年竞选连任时，把自己变成了参议院中最保守的参议员。

sentences.en: That was the re-election when John McCain sort of tried to disassociate himself with the term maverick when, in fact, two years earlier,
sentences.zh: 那是约翰·麦凯恩试图将自己与“特立独行者”这个词撇清关系的连任竞选，而事实上，两年前，

sentences.en: he had based his entire presidential campaign about being a maverick.
sentences.zh: 他整个总统竞选的基础就是关于做一个特立独行者。

sentences.en: Like, people at that point were asking, what's going on with John McCain?
sentences.zh: 当时人们都在问，约翰·麦凯恩怎么了？

sentences.en: So, I think, in a sense, he was pointing out the synergy between his hero eight years ago and what he was going through today.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为，从某种意义上说，他是在指出他的英雄八年前所经历的与他今天所经历的之间的协同效应。

sentences.en: But again, that's a pretty, you know, transparent way of looking at and describing what is happening to someone when they are essentially doing political contortions.
sentences.zh: 但再说一次，这是一种非常透明的方式来看待和描述某人在进行政治扭曲时所发生的事情。

sentences.en: Lindsey Graham is, one, a good politician.
sentences.zh: 林赛·格雷厄姆，第一，是个好政客。

sentences.en: Two, someone who is fully aware of what the political reality is for him as a conservative,
sentences.zh: 第二，他完全清楚作为一名保守派，他的政治现实是什么，

sentences.en: or someone who wants to be re-elected in a very conservative state, in a very conservative party, and is someone who knows very much how Washington works.
sentences.zh: 或者是一个想在一个非常保守的州、一个非常保守的党派中连任的人，而且他非常了解华盛顿是如何运作的。

sentences.en: That he's up front about what this is and what it isn't, and the degree to which this is an opportunistic, transactional relationship.
sentences.zh: 他直言不讳地说明了这是什么，不是什么，以及这在多大程度上是一种机会主义的、交易性的关系。

sentences.en: Yeah, he would call it politics.
sentences.zh: 是的，他会称之为政治。

sentences.en: Mark, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 马克，非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you, Michael.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，迈克尔。

sentences.en: Great to be with you.
sentences.zh: 很高兴和你在一起。

sentences.en: Thank you very, very much.
sentences.zh: 非常、非常感谢。

sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Wow, I came to the right place.
sentences.zh: 哇，我来对地方了。

sentences.zh: 周末，林赛·格雷厄姆在保守派政治行动会议的年度聚会上发表了讲话，

sentences.en: where he once again praised President Trump and boasted about their close relationship.
sentences.zh: 他在会上再次称赞了特朗普总统，并吹嘘他们之间的亲密关系。

sentences.en: And I couldn't be more proud of the fact that he talks to me and he asks my opinion.
sentences.zh: 我为他与我交谈并征求我的意见这一事实感到无比自豪。

sentences.en: And we've got a lot in common now.
sentences.zh: 我们现在有很多共同点。

sentences.en: I like him and he likes him.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢他，他也喜欢他。

sentences.en: And, uh...
sentences.zh: 还有，呃……

sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.zh: 每个人都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能访问所有的报道。

sentences.zh: 周一，众议院司法委员会主席杰里·纳德勒要求与特朗普总统有关的80多名个人和组织提供记录，

sentences.zh: 因为该委员会正在发起一项广泛的调查，以确定总统是否滥用权力和妨碍司法公正。

sentences.en: The requests were delivered to Trump's business partners, White House staff, and family members, including the president's two sons, Eric and Donald Jr.
sentences.zh: 这些请求被送达给了特朗普的商业伙伴、白宫工作人员和家庭成员，包括总统的两个儿子，埃里克和唐纳德·小特朗普。

sentences.en: And they touch on everything from the president's payments of hush money to women to his financial dealings with Russia.
sentences.zh: 它们涉及从总统向女性支付封口费到他与俄罗斯的金融交易等方方面面。

sentences.zh: 总统先生，你会配合纳德勒先生吗？

sentences.zh: 周一在白宫，特朗普被问及这项新的调查。

sentences.en: It's all a hoax.
sentences.zh: 这一切都是骗局。
